items.item: ground veal (or lamb, turkey, or chicken)
Carolina extra long grain white rice

items.prep: separate, not from the pot sauce cans

items.item: white pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder

items.prep: the other half of the prepared onions

instructions: Freeze the 3 medium cabbage heads for about 3 days, then transfer to a tray or bowl in the refrigerator to thaw for 24 hours or more, until completely thawed and the leaves separate easily.

Separate the leaves and discard dirty or damaged leaves and the very green outer leaves; prefer the pale inner leaves for rolling. Squeeze out excess liquid. Shave down the thick, fibrous rib at the bottom center of each rolling leaf so it is thinner and more flexible, without cutting through the leaf.

Chop and fry the 4 onions in the oil, then divide equally between the filling and the pot; let the filling onions cool. Gently combine the beef, ground veal, dry rice, 1/4 cup cold water, 2 fried onions, eggs, sugar, honey, 2-3 tbsp tomato sauce, honey Dijon, sriracha, salt, white pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder. Mix only until evenly combined; do not knead into a smooth paste.
Place filling on a prepared leaf, fold the sides over it, and roll closed. Keep the rolls reasonably similar in size.

Reserve enough good whole leaves for about 22-24 rolls. Chop all remaining usable cabbage for the pot. Once the leaves are all prepared, finish rolling the remaining filling before constructing the pot.

Build three layers: start each layer with chopped cabbage and sauerkraut plus its liquid, add rolls, then add a third of the sauce ingredients, water, sugar, and seasonings. Place one marrow bone at the bottom and the second in the middle layer, if using.

Bring the pot to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 3-5 hours, starting to check at 3-3 1/2 hours. Check the meat with a thermometer in the center of a large roll: at least 160°F for beef, veal, or lamb, or at least 165°F for turkey or chicken; check more than one roll. Split a roll open to confirm the rice is fully soft without a hard center and the cabbage is tender, then taste and adjust seasoning.
notes: Plan ahead: freeze the cabbage about 3 days, then thaw 24 hours or more in the refrigerator. 'Scant' means slightly less than stated. The 1/4 cup filling water is a new addition; the cooked-rice option is untested in this recipe. Yield and cooking time are approximate.
